transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10 09:30 PT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maria Gomez (Redwood SE), Dr. Ethan Park (MedArchive Head Eng), Sana Rahman (MedArchive ML Infra), Claire Donovan (MedArchive Compliance)

Summary (auto): go/no-go thresholds agreed with small tweaks; will run a two-week pilot focusing week-1 latency/functional baseline and week-2 scaled load + quality gating. Reporting will be a single benchmark packet (CSV + PDF) and Grafana links.

-- Transcript body --
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone good morning, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda — confirm success criteria, confirm workload, and lock the acceptance reporting format. does that sound right?
[00:07] Dr. Ethan Park: yeah that's perfect. we have Claire on to make sure compliance needs are baked in.
[00:10] Claire Donovan: hi all, yep, i'll flag anything that will block signoff.
[00:14] Maria Gomez: i'll drive the benchmark runbook and dashboards, alex will handle contract/pricing followups.
[00:18] Sana Rahman: also want to confirm we can run a mixed workload: short clinical-extract prompts and longer summarization prompts, and some synthetic high-throughput traffic.
[00:25] Alex Chen: perfect, so let's start with acceptance thresholds. we propose go/no-go gates that are both performance and quality. from our side the draft is: p50 tokens latency under 120ms, p95 under 350ms, sustained throughput target 180-220 qps on dedicated pool, 99.5% availability during runs, and error rate less than 0.2%. for quality, extraction F1 > 0.88 on your labeled set and summary ROUGE-L > 0.62. does that line up with expectations?
[00:52] Dr. Ethan Park: the latencies look reasonable, p95 at 350ms — acceptable. throughput wise 200 qps is our upper target; in production we might not need steady 200 but the POC should demonstrate headroom to 200.
[01:08] Sana Rahman: quick clarification — how are you measuring token latency vs request latency? we need to make sure tooling lines up for our internal SLIs.
[01:15] Maria Gomez: good question. we'll capture per-request and per-token metrics. our CSV contains columns: request_id, route, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_latency_ms, tokens_per_second, model_variant. the p50/p95 stated are on total request latency for the default route. we can add token-level percentiles in the artifact.
[01:33] Claire Donovan: for compliance, we need detailed audit logs for any data that touches PII during the test — KMS key ids, de-identification steps, and retention TTLs. can redwood provide an export of audit logs in a format our auditors accept?
[01:45] Alex Chen: yes — we can include audit log export (JSONL), with request timestamps, model version, and KMS key thumbprint. note: if you run on Redwood Private (VPC), logs can be pushed to your S3 with your own KMS. for hosted, we provide an encrypted export.
[01:58] Dr. Ethan Park: good. about the quality checks — Sana is going to give us a 1k labeled sample for extraction and 200 summaries for ROUGE. we'll use those as the canonical evaluation sets.
[02:09] Sana Rahman: i'll upload as JSONL and share a short schema. one ask — what's the expected noise in transcription? i mean the test harness will be deterministic but the model outputs can vary. do you do multiple seeds?
[02:18] Maria Gomez: we capture N=3 seeds for generation (where applicable) and compute median/mean metrics. for extraction tasks that are deterministic we run single pass. we'll include variability columns in CSV.
[02:27] Alex Chen: ok moving on to workload sizing. we propose two phases: baseline (week 1) and scale (week 2). baseline: run the canonical dataset at low concurrency to measure functional correctness and p50/p95. Scale: replay real-traffic traces at 1x, 2x, and 4x expected traffic to exercise autoscaling and fallbacks.
[02:45] Dr. Ethan Park: timeline wise we'd like the POC to start 2026-09-20 and finish 2026-10-03. week 1 for baseline + functional acceptance, week 2 for load and regression checks, then 2 business days for reporting. is that feasible?
[02:59] Maria Gomez: yes that's doable. recommend we schedule the benchmark kickoff on 2026-09-21 (slot TBC). I'll send two times.
[03:06] Sana Rahman: for the scale tests, we need control over KV cache population to reflect warm and cold-start behavior. can Redwood seed the KV cache or do we need to craft requests?
[03:15] Maria Gomez: we can seed the prefix cache and provide scripts to warm KV cache; we also provide a cold-start sweep. in the runbook i'll include curl/python snippets that exercise the same keys. note: our K-V cash (laugh) — sorry, KV cache — behaves slightly differently across quantized model variants, and we'll call that out.
[03:34] Claire Donovan: small red flag: if logs contain PHI we need to ensure they're redacted before any external transfer. would you accept us running in your Private offering with logs staying in our bucket?
[03:44] Alex Chen: absolutely. Private deployment with customer-managed S3 + KMS keeps logs in your environment. for hosted we can provide a filtered export or sign a narrow TPA for the POC.
[03:54] Dr. Ethan Park: ok about acceptance reporting format — what will you deliver?
[03:58] Maria Gomez: deliverables: 1) Benchmark CSV packet (per-request rows + aggregated metrics); 2) PDF report with executive summary, pass/fail table per gate, plot suite (latency percentiles, error rate over time, throughput curve); 3) Grafana dashboard links and raw Prometheus dumps; 4) a short runbook with reproduction steps and exact commands used.
[04:18] Alex Chen: and one more thing — we propose a simple pass/fail rubric: each gate is either hard fail (blocker) or soft fail (requires discussion). hard fails we call immediate go/no-go blockers: p95 > 450ms, error rate > 1%, or extraction F1 < 0.80. everything else is soft fail. does that escalation model work?
[04:35] Dr. Ethan Park: yes that's clear. why the p95 450 hard fail vs the 350 target? just to be explicit for go/no-go.
[04:42] Maria Gomez: the 350ms is our target; 450 is the outer threshold where experience is unusable. helps avoid noise from transient infra events.
[04:50] Sana Rahman: about variability — can you include host-level CPU/GPU utilization and per-shard latency? our infra team will want to map hotspots.
[04:58] Maria Gomez: yes, we'll include per-instance metrics (GPU util, mem usage) in the Prometheus dump and annotate spikes in the PDF.
[05:06] Claire Donovan: one compliance question — are the model weights in scope for export? we can't have model artifacts leave the box for IP reasons.
[05:12] Alex Chen: for Redwood Private, we don't export model weights. for hosted we use model variants in our catalog; no weights are shared. we can sign an NDA addendum if needed but usually weights never leave our managed infra.
[05:25] Dr. Ethan Park: good. on reporting cadence — we expect the initial baseline PDF within 48 hours of week-1 completion, and a final packet 48 hours after week-2. is that ok?
[05:34] Maria Gomez: yes, we'll aim for 48-hour turnaround. the final packet will include a pass/fail table and a recommended next steps list (e.g., config changes, batching/quant options).
[05:44] Alex Chen: quick note on model variants — we'll run the POC on two variants: a quantized 8-bit high-throughput variant and a 16-bit low-latency variant. we'll show a cost/latency tradeoff in the PDF.
[05:56] Sana Rahman: for the quantized variant, please note any increased token-level hallucination rate. we will include a small manual review sample.
[06:05] Maria Gomez: yes we can add a sampling table of 'manual checks' where your SME reviews 50 outputs and we surface discrepancy rates.
[06:12] Dr. Ethan Park: what about authorization and RBAC for the POC? our team will need scoped accounts for run control.
[06:18] Alex Chen: we'll create two API keys: a read/observe key for engineers and a run key for SE-run tests. For Private we can map to IAM roles, and for hosted we'll provide scoped service accounts with SSO support (SAML).
[06:30] Claire Donovan: we also need evidence of SOC2 controls around deployment and change management during the POC. can you include a short attestation?
[06:36] Alex Chen: yes, we'll send the SOC2 summary doc and a one-page attestation for the POC period.
[06:41] Sana Rahman: ok last thing — reporting format specifics: the CSV schema you mentioned — can you paste an example row in the playbook? we want to plug it directly into our analysis scripts.
[06:50] Maria Gomez: absolutely. example row: request_id, route, input_tokens, output_tokens, model_variant, total_latency_ms, p50_token_latency_ms, p95_token_latency_ms, error_flag, quality_score, seed. we'll include column docs in the spreadsheet.
[07:06] Dr. Ethan Park: sounds good. any other blockers?
[07:09] Claire Donovan: just a note — our auditors want to see the KMS key ARNs and TTLs before test start. I'll put that in an action item.
[07:17] Alex Chen: noted. we will provide example KMS metadata for Private and hosted scenarios.
[07:21] Maria Gomez: ok, i'll summarize the acceptance gates here so we have them in chat:
[07:25] Maria Gomez (reading): Target gates: p50 < 120ms (target), p95 < 350ms (target), throughput >= 180 qps sustained (target). Hard-fail gates: p95 > 450ms, error_rate > 1%, extraction F1 < 0.80. Quality gates: extraction F1 >= 0.88 preferred, ROUGE-L >= 0.62 preferred. Logging: audit logs and JSONL export required for any PHI touched. Reporting: CSV packet + PDF + Grafana links + runbook.
[07:55] Sana Rahman: thanks, that matches our notes. one small ask — can you capture tail latency per-route? we have some routes that are long form and others that are short.
[08:02] Maria Gomez: yes, per-route percentiles included.
[08:05] Alex Chen: great. i'll send the benchmark playbook and spreadsheet template by Monday (2026-09-13). Maria will propose kickoff slots for 9/21. Sana will share datasets by 9/14. Claire will confirm compliance checklist by 9/16.
[08:19] Dr. Ethan Park: perfect — after the final packet we'll have a go/no-go review call the week of 10/05.
[08:25] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with a concise email with attachments and links.
[08:28] Claire Donovan: thanks all.
[08:30] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription substituted 'K-V cash' for KV cache in one spot, occasional speaker attribution errors.

Pass/Fail rubrics (one-liner recap):
- Soft pass: within 10% of target, needs optimization plan
- Hard fail: beyond threshold (p95>450ms, error>1%, F1<0.80) => block signoff
